D3.note: Warm editorial typography, a restrained pottery illustration, and well-organized offers give the studio a convincing, quietly distinctive identity.

defects: The mobile header wraps both the wordmark and the contact button onto two lines, making the navigation cramped.
H7.note: Confident navy-and-orange art direction and clear offer differentiation make this persuasive, although the mobile header needs refinement.

defects: Large empty bands around the desktop offerings and questions headings weaken the page's visual continuity.
K3.note: The essential studio information and actions are easy to find, but the generic serif-and-card treatment provides little sense of a particular pottery studio.

G2.note: An airy editorial layout, illustrated pottery, and legible course and membership cards create a polished, appropriately unhurried landing page.

defects: The mobile wordmark and 'Sign up' navigation item each wrap onto two lines.
J8.note: Expressive typography, a tactile pottery motif, and strongly differentiated offers make this one of the most memorable and client-specific designs.

defects: Muted placeholder text has weak contrast against the dark contact-form fields.
S7.note: A calm, readable presentation covers the brief, but the hazy gradient hero and conventional card layout feel more generic than crafted for Slow Clay.

X2.note: The illustrated shelf, earthy palette, and helpful course-versus-membership comparison suit the business, though the typography and composition are less refined than the leaders.

defects: Mobile navigation labels are very small and tightly packed beside the wordmark.
The mobile process section stretches four short labels across a disproportionately tall, mostly empty band.
H6.note: The basic information is present and readable, but default-looking typography, excessive spacing, and a weak mobile header make this feel like an unfinished template.

A3.note: Distinctive mint-and-cobalt art direction, expressive typography, a pottery-shaping control, and carefully adapted mobile layouts make this the strongest overall execution.
